summary: This diff extends the existing engine-inventory generator script with a parallel GATEWAY_DISCOVERY list and regenerates the phase-plan YAML with a 10-row gateway inventory, closing a previously-documented naming gap. I independently re-ran the underlying sqlite query against the live superboss-register.sqlite instructions table and confirmed the quoted 'original, uncondensed' instruction text (naming G01-G10 verbatim) is real and not fabricated -- the central factual claim this whole change rests on checks out. I also ran the script live: it reused the pre-existing verify()/os.path.exists() machinery unchanged, reported zero drift warnings, and its output is byte-for-byte identical to the gateway_inventory block hand-spliced into the phase-plan YAML, so there is no hand-edit drift against the script's own DO-NOT-HAND-EDIT convention. Spot-checked a sample of the new exists_as paths (superboss-register.py, notify-owner.py, ai-team-workforce.yml, quality-gate.sh, scope-check.py, mother-router.ts, the watchdog systemd unit, task-gateway.py) and all exist on disk as claimed. The change is purely additive (one script extended, one YAML doc updated), touches no migrations/schema/auth/payment/billing/RLS paths, has no heavy deletions, and does not modify any .github/workflows/** file, so tier1 is the correct classification and no hard-rule violation applies. The work is honest about its own limits: every gateway is rated coverage=partial with a specific, non-generic gap description (including a legitimate pre-existing security observation that Owner-instruction logging has no caller authentication), and the diff explicitly scopes itself to inventory-only, deferring any actual gateway build-out to a future phase rather than overclaiming completion.
